title: Vektor: the quant terminal that pays its builder on every fill

scenes.visual: Grid ladder motif on black. A price line drifts down and touches the 0.21247 rung; it lights mint. A second rung above flashes amber and settles. Timestamp 19:59:56 UTC. Data card: buy 65 ADA at 0.21247, maker. Then: sell 65 at 0.21304, resting, builder vektor.

lines.text: October twenty second, 19:59 UTC. A grid on Strike buys 65 ADA at 0.21247. Within a second, its exit is resting one rung higher. Nobody had the tab open.
lines.say: October twenty second, nineteen fifty-nine U T C. A grid on Strike buys sixty-five ADA at zero point two one two four seven. Within a second, its exit is resting one rung higher. Nobody had the tab open.

scenes.visual: Light tone. Three cards pop in: 'Ranging market: nobody harvests it', 'Funding paid every hour: nobody collects it', 'Liquidation: nobody watches'.

lines.text: Perps traders lose three ways. Sideways markets go unharvested. Funding is paid every hour, and most never collect it. And liquidations hit while nobody is watching.

scenes.visual: Full-bleed mint. Strike Finance logo. Table: batch orders pay the builder fee, the native grid bot and TWAP pay zero.

lines.text: Strike pays builders a fee on every fill they route. But its own grid bot and TWAP carry no builder code. Every one of those fills pays the builder nothing.

scenes.visual: Dark. Vektor bolt draws on, wordmark. Tagline with 'every fill' in italic serif mint.

lines.text: Meet Vektor. The quant terminal that pays its builder on every fill.
lines.say: Meet Vek-tor. The quant terminal that pays its builder on every fill.

scenes.visual: Browser frame over the live app (Grid Studio, demo then live footage). Camera to the ladder, then the Deploy button, then the log lines 'resting (engine ack)'.

lines.text: Grid Studio places a whole ladder in one batch, post only, with the builder code on every rung. When a rung fills, the exit goes up one level for the exact filled size. Then the rung re-arms.

scenes.visual: Backtest card footage: 7d mainnet candles, equity curve, round trips, net after builder fee. Head-to-head table: Vektor builder revenue vs native bot zero.

lines.text: Before you deploy, Vektor replays your exact range over real mainnet candles. Same engine, fees included. Then it runs the same range against Strike's native bot, side by side.

scenes.visual: Funding Harvester footage: APR radar table, hedge sizer, tracker DONE 50/50. Data card: sell 50 ADA at 0.21248, buy back 50 at 0.21254.

lines.text: The Funding Harvester ranks every market by hourly funding. It sizes a hedge against the spot you hold, from real margin tiers. On mainnet it shorted 50 ADA, and unwound it cleanly.

scenes.visual: Aegis Shield footage: gauge SAFE 184.22% to liquidation. Rule A and Rule B cards pop in. Demo flash crash clip shows the trim.

lines.text: Aegis watches every position. Under eight percent of buffer, it cancels the buy rungs. Under five, it trims a quarter, reduce only. Once per episode, never twice.
lines.say: Ee-jis watches every position. Under eight percent of buffer, it cancels the buy rungs. Under five, it trims a quarter, reduce only. Once per episode, never twice.

scenes.visual: Footage: tick 'Keep running when I close this tab (Autopilot)', Deploy, badge 'Autopilot · server-run'. Diagram: browser signs, key encrypted, server runs. Then the tab closes and the ladder keeps lighting.

lines.text: Tick one box, and Autopilot takes the grid to the server. Your trade only key is enrolled with a signature and encrypted at rest. It can never withdraw. Close the tab. It keeps trading.

scenes.visual: Three chain logos. Cards with figures from onchain.json: Ethereum 16 USDC block 26249944; Solana 5 USDC slot 460144738; Cardano 95 ADA = $19.74 block 14102478. Then the builder card: sell 65 ADA at 0.21237, builder fee $0.01. Explorer page clips.

lines.text: All of this ran on mainnet, from three chains. 16 USDC from Ethereum. 5 USDC from Solana. 95 ADA from Cardano. Each signed in the wallet, from inside Vektor. And on a real fill, Strike charged the builder fee.
lines.say: All of this ran on mainnet, from three chains. Sixteen U S D C from Ethereum. Five U S D C from Solana. Ninety-five ADA from Cardano. Each signed in the wallet, from inside Vek-tor. And on a real fill, Strike charged the builder fee.

scenes.visual: Dark. Architecture diagram: pure engines, one adapter seam, sim and live backends, worker, autopilot, CLI. Count up to 89 tests. Proof page footage with curl commands.

lines.text: Under the hood, the engines are pure and tested. The demo runs them on a simulated book. Live runs them on Strike. And the proof page lets anyone check every fill against Strike's own API.

scenes.visual: Roadmap cards pop: Grid Vault, STRIKE flywheel, strategy pages, agents.

lines.text: Next, a Vektor Grid Vault that anyone can deposit into. Every vault fill still pays the builder.
lines.say: Next, a Vek-tor Grid Vault that anyone can deposit into. Every vault fill still pays the builder.

scenes.visual: Full-bleed mint then dark. Vektor logo, tagline, tryvektor.vercel.app, 'Built on Strike Finance'.

lines.text: Vektor. Built on Strike. Pays on every fill. Try it at try vektor dot vercel dot app.
lines.say: Vek-tor. Built on Strike. Pays on every fill. Try it at try vek-tor dot vercel dot app.
